chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not befitting that you wear a loin cloth loosely above the shirt while you are praying, nor wear the trouser on top of the shirt when you are praying, for it is from the adornments of the pre-Islamic period.

key_terms.تَتَوَشَّحَ: To wear or adorn oneself (specifically with the izar)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing the izar loosely over the shirt during Salat?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the practice of wearing the izar loosely over the qamis as a distinctive fashion of the Jahiliyyah, thereby linking physical attire to spiritual authenticity. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying acts of worship from cultural affectations of ignorance, ensuring that the believer's appearance reflects modesty and distinct Islamic identity rather than pre-Islamic vanity.
